implementation.summary: MirrorIntent.ResolveAndSend routes to a real resolveAndSend(): canSend guard, then a SEPARATE currentFrozenHeld guard reducing SendPhase.Failed plus a Kermit warning, then Preparing -> off-main assembly -> Publishing -> handoff.publish, timed with the injected elapsed seam. Success reads the count off the frame that was sent (pre-reset by construction), reduces Sent, resumes live unless MirrorSession.Lost (SC-27, where it only empties the batch), and posts SendComplete with toastLabel. Failure reduces Failed and touches nothing else, so UnsupportedAnnotationHandoff.publish throwing on Android/iOS is a visible failure rather than a crash. Refactor: clearStaged's body became a shared MirrorUiState.withoutStagedBatch() used by both clear and the Lost-session success path.

It compiled and passed tests because T-5's HandoffSourcesProviderTest registers the provider in a throwaway module, stepping over the real graph. Fixed here.

troubleshooting.issue: FOR T-10: SendPhase is left terminal (Sent/Failed) after a send - nothing resets it to Idle. canSend is unaffected (neither value is in-flight), but if the status overlay is driven off send != Idle, the UI needs its own dismissal or T-10 must add a reset intent.
FOR T-10: on a Lost-session success the frame stays pinned with an empty batch, so the Resolve & Send button correctly goes disabled while the frozen frame is still on the stage.

TAC-7's test is only weakly probative, as the red author stated plainly: it shows the work avoided the thread driving Orbit's pinned test dispatcher, but a correct implementation could satisfy it by hopping to any dispatcher. The real guarantee was confirmed by source review (see the AS-30 validation entry), not by the assertion.
